wing:
title Why can a plane fly?
draw wing 180x120
slider p 0..1 = 0 hidden
curve top 4,42 40,26 85,22 125,32 176,48 arrow --dashed color=blue
curve low 4,90 60,88 120,84 176,80 arrow --dashed color=blue
blob foil 22,66 34,54 62,47 98,49 150,62 98,67 56,70 30,70 hatch=gray ~ wing
repeat i=0..3: circle up{i+1} 0,0 2 fill=blue along=top@0.06+0.08*i+0.6*p
repeat i=0..3: circle down{i+1} 0,0 2 fill=blue along=low@0.06+0.08*i+0.35*p
arrow lift 72,45 72,4 width=2 stage=2 !accent
text liftlabel 82,12 lift stage=2
arrow weight 72,72 72,118 width=2 stage=3 ~ weight
arrow drag 152,64 176,64 stage=3 ~ drag
step Air splits: The wing cuts the oncoming air in two streams. | wing[foil] wing=1 p=0
step Top is faster: Air over the curved top has to hurry and races ahead. | wing[top] p=1
step Lift: Fast air pushes less, so the wing is pulled upward. | wing[lift] wing[liftlabel] wing=2
step Balance: Lift beats weight, the engines beat drag. The plane flies. | wing[weight] wing[drag] wing=3

systems:
title What happens when you open a web page
subtitle From typing a URL to a rendered page, in about 200 ms
dir right
group device Your device
group cloud Cloud
browser Browser @globe in device ~ Turns the URL into requests and draws the page
dns DNS @book-open ~ The internet's phone book: domain name in, IP address out
cdn CDN @simple-icons:cloudflare ~ Servers near you that keep copies of files, so most requests never travel far
server App server @simple-icons:nodedotjs in cloud !accent ~ Your code: builds the response for everything the CDN does not have
cache Cache @simple-icons:redis in cloud ~ Memory for recent answers, much faster than the database
db Database @simple-icons:postgresql (cylinder) in cloud ~ Where the data lives for good
browser --> dns lookup
browser -> cdn HTTPS
cdn -> server cache miss
server -> cache
server -> db
step Find the address: DNS turns the domain into an IP address. | browser dns browser->dns
step Nearest edge: a CDN close to you answers from its cache. | browser cdn browser->cdn
step Cache miss: only what the CDN lacks reaches your server. | cdn server cdn->server
step Fetch the data: the server reads the cache first, then the database. | server cache db server->cache server->db
pictures:
title A packet travels through the network
draw net 160x80
slider p 0..1 = 0 hidden
curve wire 15,55 50,25 110,60 145,25 --dashed
object laptop 15,62 22 ~ Client
object server 145,18 26 ~ Server
circle pkt 0,0 4 fill=accent along=wire@p
step Leaves: The packet starts at the client. | net[pkt] p=0
step On the way: Routers forward it hop by hop. | net[pkt] p=0.5
step Arrives: The server receives the packet. | net[pkt] p=1

code:
title How Sketchy draws a scene
subtitle Hover a box to see what it does
dir right
group src src/ (MCP server)
group viewer viewer/ (in the chat)
server server.ts in src !accent ~ The MCP server: receives the sketch call from the AI
builder builder.ts in src ~ Checks the scene: ids, references, parts
layout layout (ELK) in src ~ Decides where every box and arrow goes
main main.ts in viewer ~ Runs inside the chat and receives the laid-out scene
render render.ts @pen-tool in viewer ~ Draws it all by hand with rough.js
server -> builder
builder -> layout
layout -> main laid-out scene
main -> render
circuit:
title ESP32 room monitor
subtitle Motion alarm with temperature and humidity sensing
part esp esp32-devkit-v1 ESP32 DevKit
part dht dht22 DHT22
part pir pir-motion-sensor PIR sensor
part bz buzzer Buzzer
part led led color=green Status LED
part r1 resistor value=220 220 Ω
wire esp.D4 -> dht.SDA green
wire esp.3V3 -> dht.VCC red
wire esp.GND.1 -> dht.GND black
wire esp.D27 -> pir.OUT yellow
wire esp.VIN -> pir.VCC red
wire esp.GND.2 -> pir.GND black
wire esp.D25 -> bz.2 green
wire esp.GND.2 -> bz.1 black
wire esp.D2 -> r1.1 orange
wire r1.2 -> led.A orange
wire led.C -> esp.GND.1 black
label pir.OUT HIGH on motion → interrupt on D27
label dht.SDA one-wire data, read every 2 s
label bz.2 PWM tone from D25
